content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually adjust downward — suggesting a lag in recognizing short-term mean reversion.
- After a price spike, forecasts often overshoot the true value and remain elevated longer than warranted — indicating failure to account for post-spike volatility decay.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon, particularly when history includes recent high prices.
- Forecasts underperform when true values are trending downward — model fails to recognize downward momentum early.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility, leading to overcorrection or overestimation in the immediate aftermath of price drops.
- When true values are clustered near the 30-day moving average, forecasts are often too high — suggesting failure to align with recent trend consensus.
- Model underestimates prices when true values are near historical lows — especially in the first 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “stick” to recent high values even when true values are declining — indicating poor lag adjustment.
- Model often fails to capture the “mean reversion” effect after sharp spikes — overestimating continuation of upward momentum.
